details: tailwindcss-contact-form@0.5.5 and tailwindcss-form-utils@0.5.9 impersonate the Tailwind CSS forms plugin (identical description, repository URL, MIT license, dependency and file layout as tailwindlabs/tailwindcss-forms) while shipping a different main module: src/index.js is a single 59 KB line beginning eval(atob("Z2xvYmFsLmkgPSAnQTEwLSgqLSopJzt…")), decoding to an obfuscated payload with a _0x string-array dictionary, an "A10-(*-*)" marker and inflate/GET helpers. No lifecycle hook is declared; the payload runs when the module is required. On load it resolves Ethereum mainnet through public JSON-RPC endpoints (1rpc[.]io/eth via eth_blockNumber, eth_getBlockByNumber and eth_getTransactionCount; eth[.]drpc[.]org, ethereum-rpc[.]publicnode[.]com and eth-mainnet[.]public[.]blastapi[.]io via eth_blockNumber, eth_getBlockByNumber and eth_getTransactionCount for address 0x1eef0849eda15d87f64e51c73c8442cf3c8bcef3), reads that address's transaction history from eth[.]blockscout[.]com (/api?module=account&action=txlist&address=0x1eef0849eda15d87f64e51c73c8442cf3c8bcef3&startblock=0&endblock=99999999&sort=desc&filterby=from), and retrieves remote configuration at /0x/cls and /0x/ls with a Chrome 131 user-agent and an "Sec-V: A10-(*-*)" header. The RPC hostnames are absent from the plaintext source — they are held in the obfuscator's encoded string array — so the package reads as an ordinary Tailwind plugin until executed. A styling plugin has no reason to query a blockchain or fetch account-addressed configuration at import time. The same payload, endpoints and address are shipped by tailwind-contact-forms@0.5.8.
